You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From b08abbd9f5996309f021684f9ca74da30dcca36a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Quinn Tran <quinn.tran@cavium.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2018 14:29:54 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] scsi: qla2xxx: Fix ISP recovery on unload

During unload process, the chip can encounter problem where a FW dump would
be captured. For this case, the full reset sequence will be skip to bring
the chip back to full operational state.

Fixes: e315cd28b9ef ("[SCSI] qla2xxx: Code changes for qla data structure refactoring")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Quinn Tran <quinn.tran@cavium.com>
Signed-off-by: Himanshu Madhani <himanshu.madhani@cavium.com>
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>
---
 drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c | 5 +++--
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c b/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c
index 2cd2e5ccce15..1fbd16c8c9a7 100644
--- a/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c
+++ b/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c
@@ -6020,8 +6020,9 @@ qla2x00_do_dpc(void *data)
 				set_bit(ISP_ABORT_NEEDED, &base_vha->dpc_flags);
 		}
 
-		if (test_and_clear_bit(ISP_ABORT_NEEDED,
-						&base_vha->dpc_flags)) {
+		if (test_and_clear_bit
+		    (ISP_ABORT_NEEDED, &base_vha->dpc_flags) &&
+		    !test_bit(UNLOADING, &base_vha->dpc_flags)) {
 
 			ql_dbg(ql_dbg_dpc, base_vha, 0x4007,
 			    "ISP abort scheduled.\n");
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by a failure in the ISP recovery process during the unload sequence. The original logic did not account for the possibility that the device could be in the process of being unloaded, leading to a situation where a firmware dump would interfere with the full reset sequence, thus preventing the chip from returning to a fully operational state. The patch fixed this issue by adding a check to ensure that the abort process could only be executed if the device was not unloading.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>
    <text2>
    <text3>
    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by a failure in the ISP recovery process during the unload sequence. The original logic did not account for the possibility that the device could be in the process of being unloaded, leading to a situation where a firmware dump would interfere with the full reset sequence, thus preventing the chip from returning to a fully operational state. The patch fixed this issue by adding a check to ensure that the abort process could only be executed if the device was not unloading.
